intro: For work you sell by people's time or by the job: a project has a customer, a team, tasks on a board, a budget in hours and money, and a way of being billed. Approved time and milestones become invoices, and you see what each project earns and costs.
start: Set your rules and your rate card in Projects settings: what each person costs and is billed at an hour.
Make your first project with New project, with its customer, dates, budget and how it is billed.
Put your team on it and add the tasks, then press Start the work.
Ask the team to fill in My timesheet each week, and approve the weeks under Timesheet approvals.

articles.title: Start a project for a customer
articles.summary: Make the project with its dates, budget and billing, put the team and tasks on it, and move it on to the work.

steps.rest: Give it a name, a type, the customer and the project manager. Start from a template to copy its columns, milestones and tasks.

steps.lead: Set the dates and the priority,
steps.rest: then choose how it is billed: fixed price, time and materials, milestones, or non-billable.
in hours and in money, the contract value and the usual bill rate an hour. The summary shows the margin if it stays on budget.

steps.lead: Press Make a draft, or Make and plan it.
steps.rest: Nothing is shared until you move it to planning.

steps.lead: On the Overview tab, press Add to the team
steps.rest: for each person, and New milestone for the points the customer must accept.

steps.lead: On the Tasks tab, press New task
steps.rest: for each piece of work, with its estimate, who has it and its due date. Move cards across the board as the work goes.
The team can now log time on it. Later, Complete the project and Close the project finish it.

tips: Your rules in Projects settings decide what a project needs before each step, such as a manager before planning, or every task done before it is completed.
Save a project you repeat with Save as a template, from its Actions menu.
Put on hold and Cancel the project each ask for a reason.

articles.title: Log time and approve the team's timesheets
articles.summary: Each person fills in their week and sends it; an approver checks it and approves it or turns it back.

steps.rest: from their menu, presses Add a row and types the time into each day, such as 1.5, 1:30 or 90m. Or they press Start the timer.
It is locked until it is approved or turned back.
and chooses a week on the left, to see its hours by day and what is billable.
or say what to correct and press Turn back. Approving costs the hours at each person's rate and makes billable ones ready to invoice.

tips: Nobody approves their own week: someone else must.
Where an approval policy holds the week, its approvers decide it in their Inbox.
An approved week that is not yet invoiced can be reopened, with a reason.

articles.title: Invoice a project
articles.summary: Turn approved time into an invoice, bill a fixed price by its schedule, and take a deposit or retainer up front.

steps.rest: Waiting to be billed shows the approved, billable time and the invoice it would make.
A draft sales invoice is made, which goes through the usual approval and posting. The time is marked invoiced, so it is billed once.

steps.lead: For a fixed price or milestones, press Add an instalment
steps.rest: under Billing schedule, with an amount and a date, or tie it to a milestone. Press Invoice when it is ready.

steps.lead: For a deposit or retainer, press Add a retainer,
steps.rest: then Invoice to fund it. Approved time is drawn from the balance first, where your settings say so.

steps.lead: To pass a cost on, press Tag a cost
steps.rest: and tick Pass on to the customer. Draw up an invoice for them under Costs to pass on.

tips: Time with no bill rate is never billed at nothing: Clafina stops and says how many entries lack one.
If an invoice is cancelled or voided, its time and costs can be billed again.
A milestone that needs acceptance is billed only once the customer accepts it.
